text:
jamie: quick question — I'm preparing a TF change to add per-AZ standby NATs for gpu-subnets and to flip route-table association to the new egress subnets. planning to do canary in staging first. main goals: avoid breaking ongoing jobs when the primary nat preempts EIP, and keep route assoc order deterministic. thoughts?

praveen: +1 for standby NATs. two quick flags: 1) we need to import existing rt_assoc resources or TF will try to recreate and transiently orphan routes. 2) check the az affinity tag we rely on in the ipam module — if it shifts, apply will attach wrong natgw.

kevin: for import you can run: `terraform import module.vpc.aws_route_table_association.gpu[0] rtbassoc-0123456789abcdef0` — but be careful, import won't change code; update the resource index to match actual association. also guard with a `create_before_destroy = true` or explicit lifecycle.

jamie: thanks. i'm worried about EIP preemption windows — we saw a previous incident where natgw lost its EIP during a zone-scale maintenance and containers started failing DNS to PrivateLink endpoints. how do we handle PrivateLink DNS fallback during NAT churn?

sasha: two options: 1) add a short-lived egress-proxy sidecar in GPU nodes to multiplex egress while NAT transitions, or 2) rely on TGW/edge fallback route to another account/region. for PrivateLink specifically, ensure resolver rules exist in the VPC for the service domain and that the route is not solely via NAT. PrivateLink traffic shouldn't need NAT if endpoints are configured correctly.

lisa-oncall: infra-bot shows a spike of NAT replace ops last month during AZ maintenance. runbook note: if scheduled maintenance overlaps with TF apply that re-associates route tables, you'll see up to ~90s of packet loss as conntrack entries drop. link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/nat-replacement (check step 2).

praveen: also check the route table tagging rule in our org-policy. We had a policy that blocks route-table-assoc changes unless `env` tag present; CI plan failed for me before because of that. Add `tags = { env = var.env }` to the association resource.

jamie: here's the minimal snippet i'm planning to apply (staging):
```
resource "aws_nat_gateway" "gpu_az" {
  for_each = toset(var.az_list)
  subnet_id = aws_subnet.egress[each.key].id
  allocation_id = aws_eip.gpu[each.key].id
  depends_on = [aws_internet_gateway.main]
  tags = { Name = "nat-gpu-${each.key}" }
}

resource "aws_route_table_association" "gpu_egress_assoc" {
  for_each = aws_subnet.gpu_subnet
  subnet_id = each.value.id
  route_table_id = aws_route_table.gpu_egress_route[each.key].id
}
```

kevin: minor: use a separate rt for canary subnet so you can flip a single subnet without touching all gpu_subnets. and add lifecycle to natgw: `prevent_destroy = false` and `create_before_destroy = true` to avoid gap.

jamie: ok i'll add canary rt and add tags + lifecycle. one more: we have a TF state lock conflict on staging state when multiple devs run `apply` concurrently. any quick mitigation?

praveen: if state lock fails, block the PR and ask the locker to unlock: `terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID>`. better: use a short apply window and encourage `plan` only for majority. we also can enable S3 object versioning + DynamoDB lock TTL to reduce stale locks.

infra-bot: CI notice: `staging/vpc` plan succeeded for branch jamie/nat-standby with 3 additions, 2 changes. No drifts detected in PrivateLink DNS records.

jamie: thanks all — i'll push updates to the branch with canary route + tags + lifecycle. please ping if you want to review the plan before i run apply (target window: tomorrow 02:00 UTC). also @lisa-oncall can you eyeball NAT replacement metrics during the canary apply?

lisa-oncall: will watch. pls post plan link here when ready and i'll put monitoring on the dashboard + pager rules if SLOs degrade. :thumbsup:

sasha: optional follow-up — if PrivateLink cross-account resolution is flaky, we might need to create an outbound resolver endpoint and attach conditional forwarders; i'll prep a short doc if that becomes necessary.

jamie: perfect, will follow up. thanks everyone!
